title: From Bytes to Bites: Examining the Online and Offline Spillover Impacts of Online Food Delivery Platform Subscriptions
eligible_reason: The design is a staggered binary adoption DiD (did = subscribe x post, with post switching on at each subscriber's own subscription date; 137 distinct daily adoption dates from 1 Aug 2019 in Table1_dateset.dta; matched never-subscribing users as controls; user and date fixed effects), but every reported regression includes seven time-varying user-level spending controls (beauty_num culture_num transport_num cafe_num housing_num mart_num medical_num) through the global varlist, including the event-study figures. Under the protocol's logged rule, a time-varying control in every reported column makes the paper ineligible as reported; recorded as a near-miss. Tables 15-16 are IV.
design_notes: User-day panel (Table1_dateset.dta: 856,152 obs, 2,162 users, 396 days from 2019-01-01 to 2020-01-31), 50% subscribers; the sample is a 1:1 matched sample built from pre-period (Jan-Jul 2019) user means (Table2.log shows balance tests before/after matching). Treatment did = subscribe * post; post = 1 from the user's subscription date (post is always 0 for non-subscribers). FE: absorb(date1 newid) with cluster(newid). Outcomes: lfocal_amount focal lfocal_byorder lcompetitor_amount competitor lcompetitor_byorder (Table 3), ltotal_order_amount total_order ltotal_order_amount_byorder (Table 4), dineout (Table 5), distance_from_home_* (Table 6, 8, 9), eat_top3 eat_nontop3 (Table 7), new_resturant (Table 10), same_check diff_check (Table 11), off_within*_dine_region_abs (Table 12). Figures 2-3: weekly event study with t_dummy (<= -8) t_6 ... t_1 t0 t1 ... t7 tdummy (>= 8) and absorb(week newid), same controls. Tables 15-16: ivreghdfe with did instrumented by sub_cumsum or august_did.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 137 distinct first post dates among subscribers (daily, from 2019-08-01) in Table1_dateset.dta.

data_files_note: README: preprocessed, anonymized analysis datasets are provided; identifiers and some variables were modified to protect proprietary information but 'preserving consistency across observations and analyses'. Not labelled synthetic. Raw transaction data are proprietary (Korean panel data provider under MOU). Matching step logs (Table2.log) are provided instead of raw data.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Near-miss: the controls-free TWFE and CSA/BJS versions could be estimated from the shipped data (user id newid, date1, did, subscribe, post), but no reported column omits the seven category-spending controls. If the protocol's time-varying-control rule is ever relaxed for 'near-miss' papers, this one is fully runnable.
